title: Flute
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS flute (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: A Boehm concert flute assembled from published data: hole positions, bore, head-joint taper, cork and mouth-hole from Boehm's 1871 treatise as recomputed and measured by Miller (1922), the embouchure riser of a measured Pearl PF-661 from UNSW, and the player's mouth pressure and jet length from a published experienced-flautist measurement (de la Cuadra et al. 2008). All sixteen holes are in the model, closed ones as hard-closed chimneys; the three notes use the published simple fingerings. Nothing was fitted to the Iowa recordings. It is a hybrid description, not one real flute, and the jet card is an interim one.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing-pressure gesture, with the lip geometry, jet length and the mouth contraction law, acting on a connected duct network (fs-couple network performance, one jet drives the whole graph)

16 tone-hole branches as plane-wave chimney sections on ideal junctions, open or closed per fingering, with the published head-joint taper as stacked cylinders, the cork cavity and the embouchure riser
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on every section of the network (moist air at the published measurement state)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the graded sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, with every open aperture and the embouchure summed at the receiver (the computed mutual operator could not be used, see below)
physics_missing: a tone-hole model beyond a plane-wave chimney on an ideal junction: no matching-volume or end-correction treatment of the junction, no pad cups, no undercut

a broadband, mutually coupled radiation model: the computed operator admits at most eight openings and is fitted to the mechanics Nyquist, where its baffled-piston quadrature fails at the clock this flute needs; the compact load holds only for ka up to 0.5 and so limits the receiver band to about 2.8 kHz, far below the flute's harmonic content; the holes also sit on a cylinder in the real flute but are placed in a flat baffle plane here

frequency-dependent loss above 3 kHz, and any loss in the tone-hole chimneys and the riser: the viscothermal cell needs rate of about fifty times its band edge, so loss is selected only on bore sections of 17 mm or more and only to 3 kHz

a jet source that speaks the played register: every flute render locks onto a single steady high-order tone (1.5 to 2 kHz) and none of these changes moves it to mode 1: authored jet gain 10 to 90, mouth pressure 250 to 550 Pa and jet length 4.5 to 8 mm (20-point map: always 3 to 10 times the target), flue height, a jet card convection ratio of 0.3 to 0.6, the jet seed, dropping the compact radiation reaction, dropping the mouth radiation. The repository's own committed single-pipe example does the same (a 0.3 m pipe with a fundamental near 550 Hz sounds its third mode at 1712 Hz), so this is the generic jet source (interim edge-tone card, authored gain, band-limited receptivity), not this flute's data. A fix for the cause found (the island's band filters added 16 theta/U of loop delay on top of the convective transit) is landed as 1718d79fb but has not run natively; until a native render sounds the played pitch this stays open
the true head-joint taper profile (only the two published endpoints are known; it is a stack of cylinders on a straight line between them) and a convergence ladder on that stacking

a flutist's lip jet: the jet card in use is the interim tonal card from a staging rig, the jet displacement gain is the demonstrator value, and the labium offset, jet angle and onset ramp are not published and are neutral or authored
breath-warmed bore gas: the bore is at the UNSW measurement state, which sits flat of a played flute
a same-specimen impedance pair, so the passive chain is checked only against the pooled UNSW statements, not against a measured impedance of this flute
wall and pad vibration, fork fingerings (F sharp, B flat), vibrato, and the register-hole and trill-hole notes

the overblown register transition: not reproduced. With the island fix, a Python mirror (not native) holds the first register from Str_W 0.27 down to about 0.05 and shows only isolated higher-register points, and where those points fall depends on the sample rate (higher register at 1800 Pa at 96 kHz but at 3000 Pa at 48 kHz). That is a numerical-convergence red flag, not a result. The published octave jump near Str_W 0.1 (de la Cuadra 2008) is therefore not claimed, and the second-register notes of the flute (A5) cannot be rendered as played yet
blocked: Rendered, but not the played note: the jet-island phase fix (1718d79fb) that should move the first register to the published Strouhal range has not run natively, and the overblown register transition is not reproduced and depends on the sample rate. Until a native render sounds the played pitch the flute, recorder, tin whistle and pan pipes remain blocked on the jet source (plan item M3.2-W4).
